description: A 100% solo-built interactive map of humanity's abandoned space artifacts. Because standard map tools only work on Earth, I coded a custom cartography engine from scratch. It projects flat planetary maps across 9 celestial bodies into a full-screen, cyberpunk HUD. Pan across planets, click glowing markers, and watch mission logs type out the history of crashed probes and rovers. Built with vanilla JS, local textures, and deep space storytelling.
summary:
For the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge, I developed an interactive, narrative-driven map documenting the discarded equipment of human space exploration. Standard mapping tools only work for Earth, so I coded a custom cartography engine from scratch using vanilla JavaScript. The application features smooth pan and zoom controls over local, high-resolution planetary maps. Clicking any glowing marker opens a mission log with a typewriter effect, revealing the history, mass, and coordinates of over 35 artifacts, from Apollo descent stages to the Opportunity rover.

This project addresses the challenge by transforming cold historical data into a cinematic storytelling experience. It is important because as we look toward The Next Frontier, we must remember our history. These abandoned sites are not space junk. They are the first monuments of our journey into the cosmos. By making this archaeology accessible to everyone, we ensure these missions are never forgotten.
details:
What it does & How it works:
"Abandoned but Not Forgotten" is an interactive, full-screen cartography app that maps the discarded equipment of human space exploration. Standard mapping libraries (like Google Maps) are locked to Earth. To solve this, I engineered a custom cartography engine from scratch using Vanilla JavaScript. It projects flat, high-resolution planetary maps onto a tactical HUD. Users can smoothly pan and zoom across 9 celestial bodies. Clicking any of the 35+ glowing markers opens a historical dossier featuring a typewriter decryption effect, exact coordinates, and mission data.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
As we look toward "The Next Frontier," it is crucial to remember the monuments of our past. These abandoned sites, from the Apollo descent stages to the Opportunity rover, are not space junk; they are the first footprints of our interplanetary journey. This project makes space archaeology accessible, engaging, and cinematic for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts worldwide.

Tools & Languages Used:
HTML5, CSS3 (Glassmorphism and CRT Scanline effects), and Vanilla JavaScript.

Creativity & Factors Considered:
I wanted to avoid a traditional, boring data table. Instead, I designed a cyberpunk "Mission Control" aesthetic. To ensure the app never lags or breaks during a presentation, all planetary maps are loaded locally rather than relying on external APIs. The typewriter effect was added to simulate a live terminal decryption, making the history feel immediate and alive.
